Save a Figure at Journal-Reference Dimensions

Source: R/helpers.R
cli_save.Rd

Saves a ggplot at the exact width (and optional height) required by Nature, Nature Communications, Science, Cell, JAMA, NEJM, Lancet, PLOS, or IEEE at print-resolution DPI. Emits publisher format compliance guidance and height checks so submission figures pass publisher gates.

Usage

cli_save(
  plot = ggplot2::last_plot(),
  file = "figure.png",
  journal = c("nature", "natcomms", "science", "cell", "jama", "nejm", "lancet", "plos",
    "ieee"),
  column = c("single", "one_half", "double", "full"),
  width = NULL,
  height = NULL,
  dpi = 300,
  units = "in",
  ...
)

Arguments

plot

A ggplot object (defaults to the last plot).

file

Output file path; the extension determines the format (pdf, png, svg, jpg, tiff).

journal

One of "nature", "natcomms", "science", "cell", "jama", "nejm", "lancet", "plos", "ieee". Ignored when width is supplied directly.

column

One of "single", "one_half", "double", "full".

width, height

Plot dimensions in inches (or in units). When NULL, derived from the journal reference specifications.

dpi

Resolution in dots per inch (default 300; use 600 for submission-ready line art).

units

Units for width/height (default "in").

...

Additional arguments passed to ggplot2::ggsave().

Value

Invisibly returns the file path.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
p = cliplot(mpg ~ wt, data = mtcars, theme = "nature")
cli_save(p, "figure1.pdf", journal = "nature", column = "double", dpi = 600)
} # }
